recipes.name: Roasted Balsamic Cauliflower
ingredients_raw: 1 head cauliflower, chopped into bite size pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Stir together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and garlic in a bowl. Add cauliflower and toss to coat. Spread mixture onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until tender, stirring occasionally, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Balsamic Cauliflower
raw_recipe.description: This roasted balsamic cauliflower recipe features florets coated in vinegar, olive oil, salt, and chopped garlic and baked in the oven at high heat.

review.reviewBody: I really think people who don't particularly like cauliflower would like this recipe...the balsamic vinegar and the caramelization from roasting add a nice sweetness. Allow about an hour to marinate for maximum flavor and don't skip the step of lining your baking sheet with foil!

Marinated at room temperature for 1 hour in a bowl, stirring occasionally. Increased olive oli and balsamic to 3 tablespoons and 4 teaspoons minced garlic. Roeasted on baking sheet lined with parchment paper at 400 for 30 minutes, stirring after 20 minutes.

Delicious! Steaming cauliflower has never produced a great flavor. This recipe did the trick! I added another tablespoon each of the vinegar and oil, and a little more salt. I marinated it for 2 hours in a large ziploc bag. I cooked it 25 minutes and it came out just right. Thanks!

This is a great base recipe to make your own. I add additional vegetables, broccoli, carrots, Brussels, lots of whole cloves of garlic, cherry tomatoes, whatever I have on hand that will hold up in the oven. I don’t necessarily measure, just season and mix in a big bowl, then let it marinate at room temp, the longer the better. Delicious hot or cold, the next day, whenever. I’ve made this dozens of times and am never disappointed.

Great recipe guide, but incorporated the readers comments. For my small head of cauliflower, next time I would increase olive oil and balsamic vinegar to 3 tbl each. Maybe consider one more clove of garlic. Marinated for 30 min minimum...mmmmm 3 adults devoured within 7 minutes upon 'almost' cooling....delicious.

What a revelation! My hubby really liked this and he doesn't care for cauliflower normally. Took others' advice and marinated it for a while, added whole peeled garlic cloves, red pepper and mushrooms. I used a very aged balsmic vinegar that is thick and sweeter than the cheaper kind and makes all the difference I think. Used cooking parchment instead of foil on the cookie tray (more environmentally friendly). Yummy and sweet. It's nothing like boiled or steamed. Can't go back now. Thank you.

Mine came out ok, and after reading reviews I can see what could have been done better. I should have marinated (not mentioned in the recipe), added a little more oil and left the garlic whole (finely chopped garlic 20 min on high definitely burns and becomes unsavory). I will try it again this way and see what happens!

This is delicious!!
Make sure you use a large enough pan so the cauliflower is not crowded and it will brown nicely.

I made this with whole garlic cloves (several) based on the other reviews and marinaded for about an hour. I think another Tbsp of olive oil would have been better. Delicious and easy! My husband said this is his new favorite way to eat cauliflower.

I made this dish for a sunday afternoon potluck dinner. I marinated it all in a bag for 4 hours then roasted it. It needed some more flavor--& I could have added fresh rosemary, as well as other veggies (after reading another review). I'll be making it again as even seasoned as it was it was good!
I added another clove of minced garlic, chopped the cauliflower small, and marinated it for 30 mins like the previous comments suggested. Super delicious! Will make again.

I made it just as written, no changes. It was easy to make but I didn't love the balsamic vinegar taste. It was just ok. I usually roast veggies with just olive oil, salt and pepper. Glad I tried it but I'll go back to my old way next time.
I am always looking for a new cauliflower recipe. This is quick, easy and healthy. Love it
Cauliflower can be pretty boring but this preparation changes the game. I didn't change anything and was pleased with the results as was the family. Will definitely make and serve again.

The only variation I made to the recipe was to chop the garlic coarsely instead of finely because of some of the comments that the garlic will burn. I was glad I did. Also, I had two types of balsamic vinegar on hand; generic and a nice one. Because of one of the comments, I went with the nicer one and it was delicious!
The taste was really surprising! Very flavorful and tender. Definitely will make it again!
It worked out well. Next time I will cut the pieces a little smaller though
